# Stacklit

> Stacklit writes a small, committable JSON index of a codebase (modules, exports, dependency edges, hints) so AI coding agents can orient themselves without re-exploring the repo each session. Free, MIT licensed, one Go binary, runs locally with no LLM and no network.

Key facts:
- Install: `npx stacklit init`, `brew install glincker/tap/stacklit`, `npm install -g stacklit`, or `go install github.com/glincker/stacklit/cmd/stacklit@latest`.
- Output: `stacklit.json` (index), `DEPENDENCIES.md` (Mermaid diagram), `stacklit.html` (interactive map), `stacklit derive` (compact text map for prompts).
- Deterministic: same repo gives the same bytes. Hard token budgets on queries (`--budget`).
- Languages: 48 languages and formats in the index. Symbol graph (query, impact, explain, slice, path, hubs) covers Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Rust and Java on master; more in progress.
- Assistants: `stacklit setup` configures 26 targets, including Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Cline, Zed and a generic AGENTS.md. MCP server via `stacklit serve` (stdio, 15 tools).
- Privacy: no telemetry, no account, no upload. The only opt-in external call is `stacklit init --summary`, which pipes names-only index data to a command the user chooses.
- Benchmarks: reproducible, no LLM calls, three pinned repos. The derived map is 137 to 1,372 tokens. The benchmark does not show a token saving over grep; it shows cheap orientation. Limitations are documented.
- Not a search engine. When the exact identifier is known, grep is cheaper.
